speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing a pruritic rash along with recent fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help narrow down the cause, can you describe the appearance of the rash in more detail, such as whether it is raised, blistering, or flat?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. The progression from prodromal symptoms to a facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a body rash, is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). To confirm this, are the lesions on her cheeks described as having a "slapped cheek" appearance, and does the rash on her trunk and extremities have a lacy, reticular pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities after a prodrome of low-grade fever and headache is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
